question: A touch sensor reads each row and each column on its own. Two fingers land at once. How many possible touch points can it compute?
answer: Four, two of them ghosts. Two rows and two columns register, and they cross at four places; the sensor cannot tell which diagonal pair is real. Such grids manage one reliable touch. Phones instead measure every crossing of a row and a column, a mutual-capacitance scan, so each finger appears where it is.
move: Totals for the rows and the columns do not fix what sits inside.
ask: What do I think I know from totals alone, when what sits inside could differ?
trap: Two fingers seem to make two readings, one each.
reference: Walker, A review of technologies for sensing contact location on the surface of a display, Journal of the Society for Information Display 20(8), 2012
